policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are allowed to create new records in any table, including the Service table, because they have Full CRUD access across all tables.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

policies.description: Any request to create or update a record must validate that all fields marked as required are present. For add_new_service the fields name and owned_by are mandatory.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Each tool call must be a single validated operation; the add_new_service call must be performed alone without bundling other unvalidated actions.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: The system must not fabricate IDs or any other data; the service ID will be generated by the API and should be used as‑is.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: If a required field for the add_new_service request is missing, the assistant must state which field is required instead of guessing or prompting for more info.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: If any of the above rules (or any other policy) would be violated by calling add_new_service, the operation must be halted and the specific policy reason returned.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role are permitted to create new Service records. Users with Manager or Agent roles do not have Create permission on the Service table and therefore must not invoke add_new_service.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.
Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: If a user attempts to call add_new_service without the required Administrator role, the assistant must halt the operation and return a 403 Forbidden response, indicating that the user role lacks authority for the operation.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: Before creating a Service record, the assistant must verify that any referenced user identifiers (e.g., the `owned_by` field) correspond to an existing and active user in the system, using the appropriate user‑lookup tools. Creation must not proceed if the relationship cannot be verified.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.
User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.

policies.description: The assistant must not ask the user for confirmation or additional permission before invoking the `add_new_service` tool; the operation should proceed directly after policy compliance checks.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.

policies.description: When optional parameters for `add_new_service` are omitted or null, the assistant must rely on the API’s default behavior and must not fabricate or assume values for those fields.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
